title: System Design for Next-Gen Frontier Models — Dylan Patel, SemiAnalysis
talk_summary: Dylan Patel explains LLM inference mechanics (prefill is compute-bound, decode is memory-bandwidth-bound) and the systems techniques labs use at scale: continuous batching, disaggregated prefill, context/KV caching, and handling noisy neighbors and stragglers.

takeaways.technique: Context/KV caching for repeated large prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Cache the KV cache of a long, reused context (e.g. a document) in CPU memory/storage instead of recomputing prefill on every query, so repeated queries over the same big context pay only for the small output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't recompute the KV cache right the the context length every single time instead you cache it
takeaways.numbers: Prefill priced ~1/3-1/4 of decode ($5 vs $15 per M tokens); a 1M-token prompt is dominated by input cost

takeaways.technique: Batch/queue work instead of batch-size-one calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Serve many concurrent requests together rather than one at a time, because running inference at batch size one wastes rented compute by 10-100x.
takeaways.evidence_quote: running batch size one you're you're going to cost yourself 10x more you know 10x is a low bar right it's actually could be 10x to 100x more
takeaways.numbers: 10x-100x more expensive at batch size 1 vs high batch

takeaways.technique: Isolate heavy/noisy workloads from latency-sensitive ones
takeaways.what_they_do: Separate compute-intensive prefill from bandwidth-intensive decode onto different accelerator pools so one heavy user (e.g. 10,000-row batch job) doesn't degrade everyone else's latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if I submit 10,000 rows to you at once that's going to kill everyone else's performance

takeaways.technique: Watch for stragglers in synchronous fan-out
takeaways.what_they_do: In synchronous workloads one slow node (a 'silicon lottery' straggler) slows the whole job; they detect and pull the slow GPU, recovering throughput.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if one of them is 10% slower then everything is 10% slower
takeaways.numbers: 25% cluster slowdown from one slow GPU on a 20,000-GPU cluster

takeaways.technique: Match workload type to the right resource class
takeaways.what_they_do: Recognize that prefill (compute-bound) and decode (bandwidth-bound) are different workloads and provision/schedule them differently even though users see one request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these are two different workloads but when you Ser when you're serving a user right ... it's one workload to them
